title: The Dog and the Sparrow variant

keywords: the dog and the sparrow variant
full_text:
A loyal sheepdog, having served a stingy shepherd until his teeth wore down, was cast out into the highway to starve. Sitting weepingly in a ditch, he was befriended by a clever sparrow who promised to feed him.

The sparrow flew into a butcher's shop, pecked a sausage from the counter, and dropped it for the dog. He did the same at a bakery, feeding his friend until the hound was full and satisfied. The dog curled up on the sunny road to take a peaceful nap.

A cruel wagoner driving a cart pulled by three horses came rumbling down the lane. The sparrow chirped a warning: "Wagoner, turn aside! My friend is sleeping there; do not crush him!"

The arrogant wagoner cracked his whip and intentionally drove his heavy iron-rimmed wheels over the sleeping dog, killing him instantly. "You have slain my friend!" cried the grief-stricken sparrow. "It shall cost you your horses and your cart!"

The sparrow pecked at the bung-hole of the wagoner's wine cask until all the fine wine drained into the dust. Then the bird perched on the horses' heads, pecking at their eyes. The furious wagoner struck at the bird with his axe, but missed every time, accidentally slaying his own three horses and smashing his wagon to splinters.

Returning home ruined and destitute, the wagoner saw the sparrow pecking at his wheat sheaves. Blinded by rage, the wagoner swung his heavy flail at the bird, striking his own stone oven and shattering his hearth, learning too late that cruelty toward the helpless breeds ruinous defeat.
moral: True friendship fiercely defends the innocent, and cruelty against the weak invites relentless retribution.
